newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 29.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - April 29.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

NEW YORK - Coca-Cola Co introduces a new worldwide advertising campaign featuring sumo wrestlers, bagpipes, a Shakespeare parody and the familiar tagline "Always Coca-Cola." The 16 new commercials use a variety of production techniques -- from animation to computer-generated special effects to live action -- to reach a broad consumer market, says a spokesman. *********

LONDON - Women are more influenced by advertising that portrays them as independent-minded and strong, but many ads remain demeaning, according to a survey of British women by Channel 4 television network.
WASHINGTON - The Supreme Court rejects a constitutional free-speech challenge to a ban on billboards that advertise cigarettes or alcoholic beverages in many public places frequented by children.

BONN - German magazines lost further advertising income to television in 1996, continuing a decade-long trend, the Association of German Periodical Publishers says. The magazine industry's net advertising income last year dropped 2.5 percent to 3.42 billion marks ($2 billion).
SERVICEROY, Utah - Iomega Corp says it has appointed Euro RSCG to handle its global advertising.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LONDON - More than a third of 15- to 24-year-olds say that new UK television station Channel 5 is not as good as expected and worse than rival channels, media research specialist CIA MediaLab says.
LONDON - Britain's Radio Authority says that a new generation of commercial digital services should hit the airwaves by 1999.

SINGAPORE - The world's first interactive broadcasting system linking television with the Internet could be a reality within a year in Singapore if experimental trials go well, the system's developer MediaManager Pte Ltd says.
PARIS - A new French weekly news magazine called Marianne launches with an anti-government satirical slant and financed independently of any established publishing group, its founders say.
SAN DIEGO, California - NetCount LLC and BPA International executives say they have formed a marketing alliance aimed at expanding adoption of standards for advertising over the World Wide Web.
NEW YORK - Prodigy Inc is expected to announce the start of an Internet service in China, through a joint venture with a state-controlled firm, the Wall Street Journal says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS, MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - It's crunch time for Mercedes-Benz AG, whose cars have long been a symbol of the upper crust establishment, as it now seeks a new type of buyer -- youthful consumers with an anti-establishment streak. The German luxury car maker says itwill soon roll out its new A-class compact car, a bid to lure customers at a younger age into the Mercedes brand.

PARIS - Euro Disney, operator of the Disneyland Paris theme park, reports its loss for the first half of the 1996/97 year widened as debt charges rose faster than operating income. The company showed a net loss for the six months to March 31, its traditional low season, of 210 million francs ($36 million), compared with a loss of 169 million for the first half of 1995/96.
SAN FRANCISCO - Expert Software Inc says it will begin shipping computer games based on McDonald Corp's characters, including Ronald McDonald, in the third quarter.

BOSTON - British Airways is offering the first 100 customers in line at its Logan Airport terminal on May 9 the chance to "pay what they weigh" for a round trip ticket between London and Boston. "The airfare on British Airways from Boston to London normally runs between $400 and $600. So anyone who weighs less than 400 pounds could save money," says a spokeswoman.
SINGAPORE - U.S. graphics-editing software company Adobe Systems Inc is making a belated move to reap Asia's growth potential, a senior company official says.

LONDON - World coffee use could fall by 1.7 percent in 1997 from 1996's 75.5 million 60-kg bags as current high bean prices suggest real retail prices this year should be 10 percent higher than in 1996, coffee analysts say.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
WARSAW - The percentage of people holding a bank account in Poland rose last year by nearly one half to 31 percent, a report released by the private Pentor polling institute shows.

LONDON - The overall volume of global music sales grew by four percent last year, totalling four billion units valued at $39.8 billion, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry says. Compact disc sales grew by nine percent while both cassette and vinyl LP sales fell by one percent and 32 percent, respectively.

BANGKOK - As students sharpen their pencils before the Thai school year begins, pawnshop owners enjoy booming business from parents trying to scrape together enough money to pay their children's school fees. Apart from valuables like gold teeth, parents pawn everyday objects like shoes, jeans and even imported whisky ahead of the new school term starting in May, a report by Thai Farmers Bank Research says.
